fullPassage: You can actually become your own cheerleader by talking to yourself positively and then acting as if you were already the person that you wanted to be. Act as though you were trying out for the role of a positive, cheerful, happy, and likable person. Walk, talk, and act as if you were already that person. Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for being the very best person in your industry or as though you had just won the lottery. You will be amazed at how much better you feel about yourself after just a few minutes of pretending.

questions.passage: You can actually become your own cheerleader by talking to yourself (A)[positively / negatively] and then acting as if you were already the person that you wanted to be. Act as though you were trying out for the role of a positive, (B)[gloomy / cheerful], happy, and likable person. Walk, talk, and act as if you were already that person. Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for being the very best person in your industry or as though you had just won the lottery. You will be (C)[disappointed / amazed] at how much better you feel about yourself after just a few minutes of pretending.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) positively(긍정적으로) (B) cheerful(쾌활한) (C) amazed(놀란) — 원문 그대로가 정답.
det.analysis:
✅ ① positively — cheerful — amazed: 자신에게 '긍정적으로' 말하고, '쾌활한' 사람을 연기하며, 기분이 나아진 것에 '놀란다'는 원문 그대로예요. ← 정답

❌ ② negatively(부정적으로)는 '긍정적으로 말하라'는 글의 핵심과 정반대예요.

❌ ③ gloomy(우울한)는 '쾌활한(cheerful)' 사람을 연기하라는 맥락과 반대예요.

❌ ④ disappointed(실망한)는 기분이 훨씬 나아진 것에 대한 반응으로 어울리지 않아요(amazed=놀란).
det.tip: positively↔negatively, cheerful↔gloomy, amazed↔disappointed 세 쌍을 구분하세요.

questions.passage: You can actually become your own cheerleader by talking to yourself positively and then acting as if you were already the person that you wanted to be. Act as though you were trying out for the role of a positive, cheerful, happy, and (A)[likable / unfriendly] person. Walk, talk, and act as if you were already that person. Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for being the very (B)[worst / best] person in your industry or as though you had just won the lottery. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) likable(호감 가는) (B) best(최고의) (C) pretending(~인 척하기) — 원문 그대로가 정답.
det.analysis:
❌ ① unfriendly(불친절한)는 '호감 가는(likable)' 긍정적 인물 묘사와 반대예요.

✅ ② likable — best — pretending: 호감 가는 사람을 연기하고, '업계 최고의' 인물인 것처럼 대하며, 잠깐 '~인 척'하면 기분이 좋아진다는 원문 그대로예요. ← 정답

❌ ③ worst(최악의)는 '최고의(best) 사람'이라는 맥락과 정반대예요.

❌ ④ complaining(불평하기)은 기분이 나아지는 원인으로 어색해요(원문은 pretending=~인 척하기).
det.tip: likable↔unfriendly, best↔worst, pretending↔complaining 을 구분하세요.

det.analysis:
❌ ① penalty(벌칙)는 '상을 받은(won an award)' 것처럼 대하라는 맥락과 반대예요.

❌ ④ debt(빚)는 '복권에 당첨된(won the lottery)' 행운의 맥락과 정반대예요.

det.korean: (A) won = 경기에서 이기다(우승하다), (B) won = 상을 타다(수상하다).
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 상을 타다 — (B) 경기에서 이기다: 두 문맥의 의미가 서로 바뀌어 있어요.

❌ ② (A) 설득하다 — (B) 상을 타다: (A)의 win the championship은 '우승하다'이지 '설득하다'가 아니에요.

✅ ③ (A) 경기에서 이기다 — (B) 상을 타다: (A) win the championship은 '우승하다', (B) win an award는 '상을 타다'로 문맥별 의미가 정확해요. ← 정답

❌ ④ 둘 다 경기에서 이기다: (B) win an award는 '수상하다'라는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: win the championship(경기 우승) vs win an award(상 수상) — 같은 won이 뜻이 달라요.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the people and activities involved in producing a particular type of goods or services"

det.korean: industry(업계/산업) — 특정 종류의 상품·서비스 생산에 관련된 사람들과 활동.
det.analysis:
✅ ① industry(업계/산업): '특정 종류의 상품이나 서비스를 생산하는 데 관련된 사람들과 활동'이라는 정의와 일치해요. ← 정답

❌ ② lottery(복권): 번호를 뽑아 상금을 받는 게임이라 정의와 달라요.

❌ ③ award(상): 성취에 대해 주어지는 상으로, '생산 활동'과는 달라요.

❌ ④ audience(청중): 공연·행사를 보는 사람들이라 정의와 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: industry = 업계/산업(특정 분야의 생산·서비스 활동 전체).

questions.passage: You will be amazed at how much better you feel about yourself after just a few minutes of __________ (pretend).
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

after just a few minutes of __________ (pretend).

det.korean: pretend(동사원형) → pretending(동명사): 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 함.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'after just a few minutes of ___'에서 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사나 동명사(-ing)가 와야 해요. pretend(~인 척하다)를 동명사 pretending(~인 척하기)으로 바꿔 'of pretending(~인 척하는 것의)'을 만들어요.
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing): of pretending.

questions.passage: Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for __________ (be) the very best person in your industry.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

an award for __________ (be) the very best person.

det.korean: be(동사원형) → being(동명사): 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 함.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'an award for ___ the very best person'에서 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 해요. be동사를 being으로 바꿔 'for being the very best person(최고의 사람인 것에 대한 상)'을 만들어요.
det.tip: 전치사(for) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing): for being.

questions.passage: You can actually become your own cheerleader by __________ and then acting as if you were already the person that you wanted to be. Act as though you were trying out for the role of a positive, cheerful, happy, and likable person. Walk, talk, and act as if you were already that person. Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for being the very best person in your industry or as though you had just won the lottery. You will be amazed at how much better you feel about yourself after just a few minutes of pretending.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: talking to yourself positively(자신에게 긍정적으로 말하기) — 자신의 응원자가 되는 구체적 방법.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignoring your own feelings(자신의 감정 무시하기): 긍정적 자기대화와 반대 방향이에요.

❌ ② copying other people(남을 따라 하기): 글의 핵심인 자기 격려와 거리가 있어요.

❌ ③ waiting for good luck(행운을 기다리기): 능동적으로 자신을 응원하라는 글과 어울리지 않아요.

✅ ④ talking to yourself positively: 'become your own cheerleader by ___'은 '~함으로써 자신의 응원자가 되다'이고, 그 방법은 '자신에게 긍정적으로 말하기'예요. ← 정답
det.tip: become your own cheerleader by ~ = ~함으로써 자신의 응원자가 되다.

questions.passage: You can actually become your own cheerleader by talking to yourself positively and then acting as if you were already the person that you wanted to be. Act as though you were trying out for the role of a positive, cheerful, happy, and likable person. Walk, talk, and act as if you were already that person. Treat everyone you meet as though you had just won an award for being __________ in your industry or as though you had just won the lottery. You will be amazed at how much better you feel about yourself after just a few minutes of pretending.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the very best person(바로 그 최고의 사람) — 업계에서 상을 받은 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a complete beginner(완전 초보자): 상을 받은(won an award) 맥락과 반대예요.

✅ ② the very best person: 'won an award for being ___ in your industry'는 '당신의 업계에서 최고의 사람인 것에 대해 상을 받았다'이므로 '바로 그 최고의 사람'이 정답이에요. ← 정답

❌ ③ an ordinary worker(평범한 노동자): 수상 맥락과 어울리지 않아요.

❌ ④ a famous athlete(유명한 운동선수): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.
det.tip: won an award for being the very best person in your industry — 업계 최고 인물로 수상.
